title: What If You Lost Your Sense of Smell Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if you woke up unable to smell anything? Food is only the start.
Smell disorders affect around five percent of people. In one survey, over nine in ten said food lost its appeal.
Many couldn't tell if food had spoiled. Over eight in ten said they were exposed to dangers like gas or rotten food.
Some people lost weight. Others ate more fatty, salty, sweet food to feel something.
More than half said relationships suffered, because shared meals stopped feeling shared.
Smell is the sense you only notice when it's gone.

description:
What if you lost your sense of smell tomorrow?
Surveys of people with smell loss find food, safety and relationships all suffer.
What should we run through next?
